beats: Same receipts. Same family. Claim them on one return and you get a hundred and sixteen dollars. On the other: three hundred and seventy-seven.
Alex earns ninety thousand, Sam thirty thousand. Together they paid thirty-five hundred dollars for dental work and glasses.
The rule: only the part above three percent of net income counts, capped at two thousand eight hundred and thirty-four dollars for twenty twenty-five.
On Alex's return, three percent is twenty-seven hundred. Only eight hundred dollars counts.
On Sam's, three percent is nine hundred. Twenty-six hundred counts.
The twist: the lower income usually wins, but only if that spouse owes enough tax to use the credit. It can't create a refund on its own.
So run both returns before you choose.
